nodes.description: mapping(address => uint256) public balance: records the ether balance credited to each investor.
mapping(address => uint256) public atBlock: records the block number of an investor's last transaction, used in profit math.
address public house: casino address that receives a 5% tip of the winnings.
function () external payable: main entry point; computes profit, plays the lottery, transfers winnings, and updates balance/atBlock.
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used as mapping key, transfer recipient, and constructor-set house.
block.timestamp: used inside blockhash(block.timestamp) as a miner-influenceable randomness source.
msg.sender.transfer(profit * 2): external ether transfer to the caller performed before state updates, enabling reentrancy.
house.transfer(winning * 5 / 100): external ether transfer to the house address with no return-value handling.
uint256 profit = balance[msg.sender] * 5 / 100 * (block.number - atBlock[msg.sender]) / 5900: unchecked arithmetic, including a block.number - atBlock subtraction.
uint256 profit: intermediate local holding the computed daily profit.
uint8 toss: branch local holding the pseudo-random lottery outcome derived from blockhash/block.difficulty/block.coinbase.
uint256 winning: branch local holding profit * 2, used to compute the house tip.

edges.reason: The caller (msg.sender) triggers the payable fallback function by sending a transaction.
balance[msg.sender] is read and written using the caller-supplied address as key.
atBlock[msg.sender] is read and written using the caller-supplied address as key.
Winnings are sent to the caller-controlled recipient address in msg.sender.transfer(profit * 2).
house is assigned directly from msg.sender in the constructor, giving the deployer privileged tip collection.
block.timestamp feeds blockhash(block.timestamp) as randomness, a miner-manipulable timestamp dependency.
balance[msg.sender] is an operand of the unchecked profit multiplication and division chain.
block.number - atBlock[msg.sender] can underflow if the stored block number exceeds the current block.number.
The fallback function executes the profit arithmetic when the caller has a non-zero stored balance.
The transferred amount profit * 2 is derived from the unchecked profit computation.
The house tip winning * 5 / 100 is derived from the unchecked profit computation.
The stored house address is the recipient of the 5% tip transfer.
transfer to msg.sender can re-enter the payable fallback before balance and atBlock are updated.
transfer to house is an external call made before the state updates, allowing re-entry.
balance[msg.sender] += msg.value updates the investor balance at the end of the fallback.
atBlock[msg.sender] = block.number records the current block at the end of the fallback.
The constructor writes the privileged house address during deployment.
The local profit value is the base of the doubled amount sent to the caller.
The local winning value is used to compute the 5% house tip that is transferred.
The toss value determines whether the winning branch inside the fallback executes.

normalization_plan.reason: profit is a local intermediate that exists only as the result of the arithmetic unsafe operation balance[msg.sender] * 5 / 100 * (block.number - atBlock[msg.sender]) / 5900, so it folds into that unsafe_operation.
toss is a function-local branch condition computed and consumed entirely inside the payable fallback, so it is normalized into the fallback function node.
winning exists only to size the 5% tip that is paid via house.transfer, so it merges into that unsafe_operation.
